title: Karnataka: Bengaluru, Mysuru, Coorg, Hampi, Badami, Gokarna and Udupi
selection: VacayOut had no Karnataka pages. This pack adds the state page and its main destinations — Bengaluru, Mysuru with Srirangapatna and Nagarhole, Coorg, Hampi, the Chalukya sites around Badami, Gokarna with Murudeshwar and Jog Falls, and Udupi — with their main sights, things to do, itineraries and guides, researched from Karnataka Tourism (Government of Karnataka) and Wikipedia.

KA1.claim: Kempegowda International Airport, about 35 km north of Bengaluru, is Karnataka's main gateway and India's third-busiest airport.

evidence.quote: it is located about 35 km (22 mi) north of the city, near the suburb of Devanahalli
The airport is the third-busiest in India

KA2.claim: Mysuru Dasara, Karnataka's state festival (Nada Habba), is a 10-day celebration ending in the Jamboo Savari procession.

evidence.quote: Known officially as Nada Habba (the state festival), Mysuru Dasara is a grand 10-day celebration.
Known locally as Jamboo Savari, this multi-kilometer royal march starts from the Mysore Palace courtyard.

BL1.claim: Bengaluru, Karnataka's capital, sits at about 900 m, which keeps it cooler than most Indian metros; it is nicknamed the Garden City and the Silicon Valley of India.

evidence.quote: Bengaluru, officially the capital of Karnataka and informally called the Silicon Valley of India
At an altitude of roughly 900 metres above sea level, the city is also blessed with a climate that remains among the most pleasant of any major Indian metro

BL2.claim: Kempe Gowda I founded Bengaluru as a planned city with a mud fort in 1537.

evidence.quote: Bengaluru’s recorded history begins in 1537 CE, when Kempe Gowda I, a feudatory chieftain under the Vijayanagara Empire, founded a mud fort on the Deccan plateau

BL3.claim: Hyder Ali planted Lalbagh in 1760; after 1799 the British took control, leaving the city split into the old 'pete' and the cantonment.

evidence.quote: Hyder Ali planted the Lal Bagh Botanical Garden in 1760
That dual identity, the ‘pete’ (old market town) and the cantonment, shaped Bengaluru’s urban fabric

BL4.claim: Classic Bengaluru breakfasts include idli-vade and filter coffee at Brahmins' Coffee Bar and masale dose at Vidyarthi Bhavan (since 1943); VV Puram food street is the city's street-food lane.

evidence.quote: Head to Gandhi Bazaar for a legendary lunch at Vidyarthi Bhavan (operating since 1943)
Dive into Bengaluru’s ultimate street-food street at Sajjan Rao Circle.

BLL1.claim: Lalbagh, begun by Hyder Ali around 1760, covers 240 acres and holds over 1,854 plant species.

evidence.quote: this historic garden spreads across 240 acres
is home to over 1,854 species of plants drawn from across the globe
Hyder Ali, the ruler of Mysore, started building this garden around 1760.

BLL2.claim: Its iron-and-glass Glass House was built in 1889 and is the centrepiece of the flower shows.

evidence.quote: This magnificent iron-and-glass structure was built in 1889 to mark the visit of the Prince of Wales to Bengaluru.
The main highlight of the Glass House is the Lalbagh flower show.

BLL3.claim: Lalbagh is open every day; on the rock inside stands one of Kempe Gowda's four boundary watchtowers.

evidence.quote: Lalbagh Botanical Garden is open every day of the year, including Sundays and public holidays.
The watchtower was one of four towers he constructed to mark the boundaries of his newly founded city.

BLC1.claim: Cubbon Park (Sri Chamarajendra Park) is a roughly 300-acre green heart of the city, laid out in 1870, with the red State Central Library and the High Court inside.

evidence.quote: the 300-acre Cubbon Park in 1870
popularly called the State Central Library, is one of the most photographed buildings in Bengaluru.
it was built in 1864 and has housed the Karnataka High Court since India’s independence.

BLC2.claim: Cubbon Park metro station is about 450 m from the Kasturba Road entrance.

evidence.quote: The Cubbon Park Metro Station on the Purple Line (Baiyappanahalli–Mysuru Road corridor) is approximately 450 metres from the park’s Kasturba Road entrance.

BLP1.claim: The Tudor-style Bangalore Palace was built in 1878 by Rev. J. Garrett and later bought by the Wadiyars; it is open 10 am to 5:30 pm.

evidence.quote: Reverend J. Garrett originally built Bangalore Palace in 1878. Maharaja Chamarajendra Wadiyar of the Mysore royal family later purchased and expanded the structure.
Bangalore Palace opens from 10:00 AM to 5:30 PM.

BLP2.claim: The palace may close on days with private events or concerts — check before you go.

evidence.quote: the palace may restrict entry on certain days, especially when it hosts private events, concerts, or exhibitions.

BLI1.claim: The Sri Radha Krishna-Chandra Mandir on Hare Krishna Hill is one of the largest ISKCON temples in the world.

evidence.quote: officially known as Sri Radha Krishna-Chandra Mandir , is one of the largest ISKCON temples in the world

BLI2.claim: It is liveliest at Janmashtami, Ratha Yatra and Vaikuntha Ekadashi.

evidence.quote: The temple is especially vibrant during major festivals like Sri Krishna Janmashtami , Ratha Yatra , and Vaikuntha Ekadashi

BLN1.claim: Nandi Hills, at 4,851 ft and about 60 km from Bengaluru, is famous for sunrise; Tipu Sultan used it as a summer retreat and fort.

evidence.quote: Situated at 4,851 feet above sea level
It is located just 60 kilometers from Bengaluru
Later, Tipu Sultan used Nandi Hills as a summer retreat.

BLN2.claim: It is open 6 am to 6 pm; September to February is the best season.

evidence.quote: Nandi Hills timings are usually from 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM every day.
The best time to visit Nandi Hills is between September and February

BLN3.claim: Tipu's Drop is a 60 m cliff viewpoint; the Yoga Nandeeshwara temple is nearby.

evidence.quote: Tipu’s Drop is a 60 metre cliff, offering breathtaking views.
Nearby is the Yoga Nandeeshwara temple on the hill.

MY1.claim: Mysuru, the 'Cultural capital of Karnataka', lies at the foot of the Chamundi Hills about 140 km southwest of Bengaluru, at about 770 m.

evidence.quote: Mysuru, often known as the “Cultural capital of Karnataka”
Situated at the foothills of the Chamundi Hills, it is about 140 km southwest of Bengaluru.
(~770 meters above sea level)

MY2.claim: The Wodeyars ruled Mysuru from 1399 until Independence.

evidence.quote: Under the Wodeyars from 1399 to Independence

MY3.claim: Mysuru is known for its palace, Dasara, silk, sandalwood and the Mysore Pak sweet.

evidence.quote: Mysuru is famous for its royal heritage, magnificent Mysuru Palace, Mysuru Dasara celebrations, traditional silk, sandalwood products and Mysore Pak.

MY4.claim: Most visitors fly into Bengaluru and drive about 3.5 hours; Mysuru Junction has daily trains from Bengaluru and Chennai.

evidence.quote: most travellers fly into Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru and continue by road, a roughly three-and-a-half-hour journey.
Mysuru Junction connects well with Bengaluru, Chennai and other major South Indian cities, with several trains running each day.

MY5.claim: October brings Dasara; November to February is quieter and pleasant.

evidence.quote: October usually brings the Mysuru Dasara festival, making it the most rewarding month to visit despite the larger crowds.
For a quieter experience with pleasant weather, aim for the cooler months between November and February.

MY6.claim: Devaraja Market is known for flowers, incense, sandalwood products and spices.

evidence.quote: Stroll through the vibrant Devaraja Market, famous for fresh local flowers, traditional incense sticks, sandalwood products, and spices.

MYP1.claim: After a fire in 1897, Henry Irwin designed today's Indo-Saracenic palace, finished in 1912; it draws more visitors than almost any Indian monument after the Taj Mahal.

evidence.quote: In 1897, a fire broke out during a royal wedding and burned the wooden palace to the ground.
Construction began almost immediately and continued for fifteen years, wrapping up in 1912
This single building draws more visitors than almost any other monument in India after the Taj Mahal

MYP2.claim: Open daily 10 am to 5:30 pm (last entry 5 pm); shoes off, and no photography inside.

evidence.quote: The palace opens daily from 10:00 AM to 5:30 PM, with the last entry allowed at 5:00 PM.
No, photography and videography are not allowed inside the palace.

MYP3.claim: About 97,000 bulbs light the palace from 7 to 8 pm on Sundays and public holidays, and for two hours nightly during Dasara.

evidence.quote: 97,000 electric  bulbs light up the palace between 7:00 PM and 8:00 PM on Sundays and public holidays. During Dasara, the illumination extends to two hours each night.

MYP4.claim: The 750 kg golden howdah, with 80 kg of gold, carries the goddess Chamundeshwari in the Dasara procession.

evidence.quote: weighs 750 kg (approx. 1,650 lbs). It is made of 80 kg of pure gold sheet encrusting a wooden frame

MYP5.claim: Mysuru Junction station is about 2 km from the palace.

evidence.quote: Mysuru Junction railway station lies about two kilometres away

MYJ1.claim: Built in 1861, Jaganmohan Palace now holds an art gallery of over 2,000 paintings, including works by Raja Ravi Varma.

evidence.quote: Built in 1861 by the Wodeyar kings, this palace once served as the royal residence before Mysore Palace was completed.
which contains over 2,000 paintings representing different schools of Indian art.
Works of Raja Ravi Varma

MYS1.claim: St Philomena's, modelled on Cologne Cathedral, is one of the tallest churches in Asia; its foundation was laid in 1933.

evidence.quote: St Philomena’s Cathedral was designed by a French architect, Daly, to resemble Cologne Cathedral in Germany.
St. Philomena’s Cathedral is one of the tallest churches in Asia.
the foundation for the new church was laid in October 1933

MYC1.claim: The Chamundi Hills, 13 km from Mysore, are topped by the Chamundeshwari Temple; a stairway of over 1,008 steps passes a giant monolithic Nandi.

evidence.quote: The Chamundi Hill is located 13 km east of Mysore
The main hill itself features an ancient stone stairway of 1,008+ steps leading to its summit
which is 4.9 m tall and 7.6 m long and carved out of a single piece of black granite.

MYR1.claim: Srirangapatna, on a Kaveri river island near Mysuru, was Tipu Sultan's capital; the fort fell to the British on 4 May 1799.

evidence.quote: Located inside a river island formed by the Kaveri
Tipu made Srirangapatna the capital of Mysore and built his power base here.
On May 4, 1799, British forces under Arthur Wellesley stormed the fort in a surprise assault.

MYR2.claim: See the Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple (c. 984 CE), the Gumbaz mausoleum and Tipu's teak Summer Palace, Daria Daulat Bagh.

evidence.quote: Srirangapatna takes its name from the Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple , which was consecrated around 984 CE .
Just outside the fort is the Gumbaz, the mausoleum of Hyder Ali, Tipu Sultan, and Tipu’s mother.
This teak-wood palace, built between 1778 and 1784, has painted frescoes showing Tipu’s battles and court life.

MYR3.claim: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary is 3 km away; October to March is the best time.

evidence.quote: The Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary , Karnataka’s largest bird sanctuary, is just 3 kilometres away
October to March is the best time to visit Srirangapatna.

MYD1.claim: Mysuru Dasara 2026 ran from 11 to 21 October, ending with the Jamboo Savari on Vijayadashami.

evidence.quote: Mysuru Dasara 2026 will begin on Sunday, October 11, 2026 , and conclude on Wednesday, October 21, 2026 .
The highlight of Mysore Dasara 2026 is the Vijayadashami parade on October 21.

MYD2.claim: Vijayanagara rulers began the festival in the 14th century; Raja Wadiyar I revived it in 1610 at Srirangapatna.

evidence.quote: Rulers of the Vijayanagara Empire originally began this celebration in the 14th century.
Raja Wadiyar I revived the grand tradition in 1610 at Srirangapatna.

MYN1.claim: Nagarhole, on the Kabini river, offers jeep and boat safaris of about 2 to 2.5 hours, twice a day.

evidence.quote: Nagarhole on the banks of River Kabini is one of the most sought forests
Each safari takes about 2 to 2 and half hours and is conducted twice a day.

MYN2.claim: In the dry months of March to May, elephants gather near the river banks.

evidence.quote: Although the scorching months of March, April and May are dry, the chances of sighting wildlife especially elephants are high near the river banks.

MYN3.claim: The forest covers 640 sq km between the Mysore plateau and the Nilgiris.

evidence.quote: The 640 sq km dense forest of Nagarhole is located between Mysore plateaus in the Karnataka region and the Nilgiris range of Tamil Nadu

CG1.claim: Coorg (Kodagu), in the Western Ghats, is called the 'Scotland of India' for its misty hills and coffee estates.

evidence.quote: Coorg, officially known as Kodagu, ranks among the most captivating hill stations in South India.
Travelers frequently call Coorg the “Scotland of India” because of its misty surroundings and scenic beauty.

CG2.claim: The Kodava community produced Field Marshal K. M. Cariappa and General K. S. Thimayya.

evidence.quote: producing legendary military leaders like Field Marshal K. M. Cariappa and General K. S. Thimayya.

CG3.claim: Madikeri is about 250 km from Bengaluru; Kannur airport (90 km) is closest, and buses run from Bengaluru, Mysuru and Mangaluru.

evidence.quote: Madikeri is 250 kms from Bengaluru city and 140 kms from Mangaluru. Kannur International Airport in Kerala is the closest to Madikeri (90 kms from Madikeri).
Madikeri has excellent bus connectivity from Bengaluru, Mysuru and Mangaluru.

CG4.claim: October to February brings cool, clear weather; the monsoon brings mist.

evidence.quote: October to February is the ideal season for visiting, with cool temperatures, clear skies, and vibrant greenery.

CG5.claim: At Dubare you can watch elephants bathe in the Cauvery; Bylakuppe, one of India's largest Tibetan settlements, has the Namdroling Monastery with 40-foot gilded Buddhas.

evidence.quote: Observe Asian elephants up close during bathing and feeding sessions
Visit Bylakuppe, one of the largest Tibetan settlements in India. Explore the serene Namdroling Monastery to marvel at its 40-foot gilded Buddha statues

CG6.claim: Raja's Seat in Madikeri is a historic garden favoured by the Kings of Coorg, known for sunset views.

evidence.quote: Head into Madikeri town to relax at Raja's Seat, a historic garden favored by the Kings of Coorg.

CGA1.claim: Abbey Falls, 6 km from Madikeri, drops about 70 ft; open 9 am to 5 pm, with a hanging bridge view and no swimming.

evidence.quote: River Kaveri drops for about 70 ft over wide rocks creating a spectacular view.
Entry to Abbey Falls is open from 9 AM to 5 PM.
Bathing or swimming in Abbey Falls is not allowed.
Abbey Falls is just 6 kms from Madikeri town.

CGO1.claim: The Omkareshwara Temple in Madikeri, built in 1820, mixes Kerala-style tiled roofs with Islamic domes; open 6.30 am–12 noon and 5–8 pm.

evidence.quote: built-in 1820 and featuring a blend of red tile-roofed Kerala architecture and Islamic-style domes.
The Temple is open from 6.30 AM till 12 noon and from 5 PM till 8 PM on all days.

CGT1.claim: At 1,748 m, Tadiandamol is Kodagu's highest peak and Karnataka's third-highest; the trek starts from Nalaknad Palace.

evidence.quote: At 1,748 m, Tadiandamol is the highest peak in Kodagu and the third-highest in Karnataka.
The trek from Nalaknad Palace, a late-1790s refuge of Kodagu’s ruler Chikka Veera Rajendra

CGI1.claim: Iruppu (Lakshmana Tirtha) Falls in the Brahmagiri Hills plunges about 170 ft, reached by a forest trail of about 1 km.

evidence.quote: the waterfall plunges about 170 feet through lush evergreen forest
The trek to the falls is moderate—about 1 km each way

CGI2.claim: The falls are weakest in the dry season (December–February).

evidence.quote: Open year-round, the falls are least impressive during the dry season (Dec–Feb)

HM1.claim: Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, founded in 1336, and among the world's largest and richest cities in the 14th–16th centuries.

evidence.quote: it was among the largest and wealthiest cities in the world during the 14th to 16th centuries.
The city’s story began in 1336, when the brothers Harihara and Bukka Raya founded the Vijayanagara Empire.

HM2.claim: Its more than 1,600 surviving monuments became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

evidence.quote: Today, Hampi’s more than 1,600 surviving monuments are protected as a UNESCO World Heritage Site , a status granted in 1986

HM3.claim: October to February is best; allow about three days. The Hampi Utsav brings dance and music to the ruins.

evidence.quote: October to February is the recommended time to visit, with about three days suggested to do the site justice.
The annual Hampi Utsav brings the Vijayanagara era to life with classical dance, music and processions amid the ruins.

HM4.claim: Hampi is about 340 km from Bengaluru; Hosapete Junction is about 13 km away and Vidyanagar airport about 40 km.

evidence.quote: It lies about 340 km from Bengaluru.
Nearest station: Hosapete Junction (13km) via Hampi Main Road
Vidyanagar airport is the closest airport (40 kms from Hampi) and has daily flights from Bengaluru and Hyderabad.

HM5.claim: On Hemakuta Hill are two monolithic Ganeshas, Kadalekalu (15 ft) and Sasivekalu (8 ft); nearby is the 22-ft Lakshmi Narasimha.

evidence.quote: Kadalekalu (15 ft) and Sasivekalu (8 ft), carved directly from living bedrock.
Stop at the fierce 22-foot monolithic Lakshmi Narasimha statue

HMV1.claim: The Virupaksha Temple is a living Shiva temple; its 9-storey east gopuram, about 50 m tall, dates from the 15th century.

evidence.quote: The main tower, on the east is an imposing structure, 9 stories, 50 meters tall, built in the fifteenth century.
At Virupaksha Temple, a nine-tiered gopuram rises above the ruins and worship continues to this day.

HMV2.claim: Inside, an inverted shadow of the main tower falls on a wall like a pinhole camera.

evidence.quote: The inverted shadow of the main tower falls on a wall inside the temple.

HMT1.claim: The Vijaya Vittala Temple has the Stone Chariot — pictured on the ₹50 note — and 56 musical pillars that ring when struck.

evidence.quote: At Vijaya Vittala Temple, the 56 musical pillars of the Ranga Mantapa ring with musical notes when struck, and the Stone Chariot in its courtyard is so iconic that it appears on the ₹50 note.

HMB1.claim: Hampi Bazaar's pillared street leads to the Royal Enclosure, with the Mahanavami Dibba, the Stepped Tank and the Elephant Stables.

evidence.quote: Once a thriving marketplace, the bazaar ran along a dedicated street flanked by pillared buildings.
This elevated flat terrain encompasses regal structures like the Mahanavami Dibba
Nearby is the Stepped Tank
come upon the impressive Elephant Stables

HML1.claim: The two-storey Lotus Mahal in the royal enclosure blends Hindu and Islamic styles; its arches resemble lotus petals.

evidence.quote: The Lotus Mahal is renowned for its Indo Islamic architectural fusion.
The arched windows and balcony resemble the petals of a lotus flower.

HMM1.claim: Matanga Hill is the highest point in central Hampi, the classic sunset climb.

evidence.quote: climb Matanga Hill—the highest vantage point in central Hampi - for a panoramic sunset across boulder hills and ruined temple complexes.

HMC1.claim: Round bamboo coracles take you across the Tungabhadra from ghats near the Virupaksha and Kodandarama temples; life jackets are mandatory.

evidence.quote: Near Virupaksha Temple, Kodandarama Temple, and Sanapur Lake
Life jackets are standard issue and mandatory for all passengers.
Rides do not require advance booking

HMC2.claim: Late afternoon and sunset are best; rides may pause during heavy monsoon.

evidence.quote: Sunset and late-afternoon rides offer breathtaking lighting and cooler breezes
Operations may be restricted or paused during heavy monsoons or strong river undercurrents.

BD1.claim: Badami (ancient Vatapi), in Bagalkot district, was the Chalukya capital from the 6th to 8th century.

evidence.quote: Tucked into the Bagalkot district of northern Karnataka, Badami served as the capital of the powerful Chalukya dynasty from the 6th to the 8th century AD. Known then as Vatapi

BD2.claim: Hubballi airport is about 105 km away; Badami has its own station, and overnight KSRTC buses run from Bengaluru (about 450 km).

evidence.quote: The nearest airport is Hubballi (Hubli), located about 105 km from Badami.
Badami has its own railway station
KSRTC operates overnight buses from Majestic Bus Stand in Bangalore to Badami

BD3.claim: October to February (18–28°C) is ideal; March to May often tops 40°C.

evidence.quote: October to February is the ideal window for visiting Badami. Temperatures stay comfortable (18°C to 28°C)
March to May brings intense heat, temperatures regularly climb above 40°C

BD4.claim: Agastya Lake lies below the caves, with the 7th-century Bhutanatha temples on its banks.

evidence.quote: This ancient man-made lake sits directly below the cave temples
a cluster of sandstone shrines dedicated to Shiva that date back to the 7th century.

BD5.claim: Try jowar rotti with ennegayi, and girmit for breakfast.

evidence.quote: Look for jowar rotti served with ennegayi (stuffed brinjal curry)
For breakfast, try the girmit, a tangy puffed rice salad

BDC1.claim: Four rock-cut cave temples, completed between 578 and 610 AD, are carved into the red sandstone cliff — three Hindu, one Jain.

evidence.quote: Chalukyan king Mangalesha completed the main complex between 578 and 610 AD.
Caves 1, 2, and 3 are dedicated to Hindu deities (Shiva and Vishnu), while Cave 4 is a Jain temple dedicated to Mahavira.

BDC2.claim: Cave 1 has an 18-armed Nataraja; Cave 3 is the largest, with some of India's earliest surviving frescoes.

evidence.quote: the first thing you see is an 18-armed Nataraja
Cave 3 is the largest, most elaborate, and arguably most beautiful of the quartet.
Some of India’s earliest surviving fresco paintings also survive on the ceiling here

BDC3.claim: The caves are open daily 6 am to 6 pm; go early or late for the light.

evidence.quote: The cave temples are open every day from 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM, including weekends and public holidays.

BDF1.claim: The fort on the north hill holds granaries, cisterns and the Malegitti Shivalaya; the climb takes 30–45 minutes and the cave ticket covers it.

evidence.quote: Inside the fort walls, you will find large stone granaries that once supplied an entire royal capital, ancient cisterns, a Buddhist cave, and the elegant Malegitti Shivalaya temple
The trek to the fort takes about 30 to 45 minutes and involves uneven stone paths
There is no separate entry fee for the fort; your cave temple ticket covers the climb.

BDP1.claim: Pattadakal, 22 km from Badami on the Malaprabha, is a UNESCO site where Chalukya kings were crowned; its Virupaksha Temple inspired Ellora's Kailasa.

evidence.quote: Pattadakal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, invites travelers to admire the grandeur of ancient temple architecture on the banks of the Malaprabha River.
Pattadakal hosted royal coronation ceremonies for Chalukyan kings.
The Virupaksha Temple inspired the famed Kailasa temple at Ellora in Maharashtra.
By Road: 22 km from Badami

BDP2.claim: The Pattadakal Dance Festival is held in January–February.

evidence.quote: Attend Pattadakal Dance Festival (Jan/Feb) for classical performances.

BDA1.claim: Aihole, the 'cradle of Indian architecture', has over 125 temples from the 4th to 12th centuries, including the apsidal Durga Temple.

evidence.quote: Aihole has over 125 temples built between the 4th and 12th centuries.
The Durga Temple here is renowned for its unique apsidal (horseshoe-shaped) design.
Often called the ‘cradle of Indian architecture’

GK1.claim: Gokarna, in Uttara Kannada, pairs the Mahabaleshwar Temple — the 'Kashi of the South' — with quieter beaches than Goa.

evidence.quote: it is home to the legendary Mahabaleshwar Temple, revered as the ‘Kashi of the South’
Unlike its glitzier northern neighbour, Goa, Gokarna has held on to a slower, more soulful pace of life

GK2.claim: Its five main beaches are Gokarna Main, Kudle, Om, Half Moon and Paradise.

evidence.quote: its five famous beaches – Gokarna Main, Kudle, Om, Half Moon, and Paradise

GK3.claim: Goa (Dabolim) airport is about 149 km away; Gokarna Road station is 10 km out, with more trains at Ankola and Kumta; overnight buses run from Bengaluru.

evidence.quote: The nearest airport is Dabolim International Airport (Goa Airport), approximately 149 km from Gokarna.
The Gokarna Road Station (GOK) on the Konkan Railway lies about 10 km from town
Multiple KSRTC and private operators run overnight sleeper buses from Bangalore

GK4.claim: October to March (20–30°C, calm seas) is best; in the monsoon the beaches close for swimming.

evidence.quote: The best time to visit Gokarna is from October to March.
Beaches are closed for swimming and water sports due to rough seas

GK5.claim: Main Beach, by the temple, is for sunsets and ritual dips — not swimming, due to strong currents.

evidence.quote: Not ideal for swimming due to strong currents.

GKM1.claim: The Mahabaleshwar Temple houses Shiva's Atmalinga and is one of Karnataka's seven Mukti Kshetras; Maha Shivaratri is its peak festival.

evidence.quote: Revered as one of the seven Mukti Kshetras of Karnataka, the temple is famous for housing the legendary Lord Shiva Athmalinga.
Maha Shivaratri is the peak festival celebrated here, drawing massive pilgrim crowds during February and March.

GKM2.claim: Open 6 am–12:30 pm and 5–8 pm, free; men must wear a dhoti (bare-chested) and women a saree or salwar — no jeans or shorts.

evidence.quote: The Mahabaleshwar Temple in Gokarna is open from 6:00 AM to 12:30 PM and again from 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM, every day of the week. There is no entry fee.
Men must wear a Dhoti/Pancha (bare-chested), and women must wear a Saree or Salwar Suit (Churidar). Jeans and shorts are completely prohibited.

GKO1.claim: Om Beach, about 6 km from town, curves into the shape of the 'Om' symbol and is the hub for water sports.

evidence.quote: The most iconic of Gokarna’s beaches, shaped naturally into the sacred ‘Om’ (ॐ) symbol
About 6 km from town, Gokarna Om Beach is the hub for water sports, dolphin-spotting boat rides, and vibrant beach shacks.

overview.text:
Karnataka packs much of South India into one state. Hampi, capital of the Vijayanagara Empire and a UNESCO site since 1986, has more than 1,600 surviving monuments; further north, Badami was the Chalukya capital, with Pattadakal and Aihole nearby. In the south, Mysuru — the 'Cultural capital of Karnataka' — is famous for its palace and its 10-day Dasara, and the coffee hills of Coorg, the 'Scotland of India', rise in the Western Ghats.

On the coast, Gokarna pairs the Mahabaleshwar Temple with quiet beaches, and Udupi, the 'Temple City', is the home of Udupi cuisine. Bengaluru, the capital, is the usual gateway.

how_to_reach.text: Most visitors fly into Kempegowda International Airport, about 35 km north of Bengaluru and India's third-busiest. From there: Mysuru is about 3.5 hours by road; Hampi is about 340 km, with the nearest station at Hosapete; Badami about 450 km, with overnight KSRTC buses; and Coorg's Madikeri about 250 km. For the coast, Gokarna is about 149 km from Goa airport, and Udupi about 60 km from Mangaluru airport.

best_time.text: October to February suits most of Karnataka: Hampi, Badami (18–28°C), Coorg and the coast. Mysuru is busiest and most festive in October for Dasara, and quieter from November to February. March to May is very hot in the north — Badami often tops 40°C. The monsoon closes Gokarna's beaches for swimming but makes Jog Falls thunder.

overview.text:
Bengaluru, Karnataka's capital and the 'Silicon Valley of India', sits at about 900 m, which keeps it cooler than most Indian metros. Kempe Gowda I founded it in 1537 with a mud fort; Hyder Ali planted Lalbagh in 1760, and after 1799 the British left a city of two halves — the old 'pete' and the cantonment.

Today you come for the gardens — Lalbagh and the 300-acre Cubbon Park — the Tudor-style Bangalore Palace, and the food: idli-vade and filter coffee, masale dose at Vidyarthi Bhavan, and VV Puram's street-food lane.

overview.text:
Mysuru, the 'Cultural capital of Karnataka', lies at the foot of the Chamundi Hills about 140 km southwest of Bengaluru. The Wodeyars ruled from here from 1399 until Independence, and the city is known for its palace, Dasara, silk, sandalwood and Mysore Pak.

Beyond the palace are the Jaganmohan Palace art gallery, St Philomena's Cathedral, Devaraja Market and the Chamundi Hills; Srirangapatna, Tipu Sultan's island capital, is a short drive away.

overview.text:

overview.text:
Mysuru Dasara — the Nada Habba, or state festival — is a 10-day celebration. In 2026 it ran from 11 to 21 October, ending with the Jamboo Savari on Vijayadashami, when an elephant carries the goddess in the 750 kg golden howdah.

The festival goes back to the Vijayanagara kings in the 14th century; Raja Wadiyar I revived it in 1610 at Srirangapatna. During Dasara the palace is lit for two hours every night.

overview.text:
Coorg, officially Kodagu, is a hill region in the Western Ghats, often called the 'Scotland of India' for its mist and coffee estates. The Kodava community gave India Field Marshal K. M. Cariappa and General K. S. Thimayya.

Madikeri is the base. Around it are Abbey Falls, Raja's Seat and the Omkareshwara Temple; further out are Dubare, where elephants bathe in the Cauvery, Bylakuppe's Namdroling Monastery, Tadiandamol and Iruppu Falls.

overview.text:
Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, founded in 1336, and in the 14th–16th centuries one of the largest and richest cities in the world. Its more than 1,600 surviving monuments became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

The Virupaksha Temple is still in worship; the Vittala Temple has the Stone Chariot and musical pillars; the Royal Enclosure holds the Lotus Mahal and Elephant Stables. Climb Matanga Hill for sunset, or float across the Tungabhadra in a coracle.

images.alt: Red sandstone cliffs and caves of Badami
images.caption: Badami

overview.text:
Badami — ancient Vatapi — in Bagalkot district was the Chalukya capital from the 6th to 8th century. Its four rock-cut cave temples were carved into the red sandstone cliff in the late 6th century; below them lies Agastya Lake with its 7th-century Bhutanatha temples, and above, Badami Fort.

Pattadakal, a UNESCO site 22 km away, and Aihole, the 'cradle of Indian architecture', complete the Chalukya trail.

how_to_reach.text: Hubballi airport is about 105 km away. Badami has its own station, and overnight KSRTC buses run from Bengaluru, about 450 km.

best_time.text: October to February is ideal (18–28°C). March to May often tops 40°C.

overview.text: King Mangalesha completed the four caves between 578 and 610 AD. Caves 1 to 3 are Hindu; Cave 4 is Jain. Cave 1 opens with an 18-armed Nataraja, and Cave 3, the largest, has some of India's earliest surviving frescoes.

overview.text:
Gokarna is home to the Mahabaleshwar Temple, the 'Kashi of the South', and keeps a slower pace than Goa. Its five main beaches — Gokarna Main, Kudle, Om, Half Moon and Paradise — are linked by a coastal trek.

Day trips run to the black rocks of Yana, Mirjan Fort, Murudeshwar's giant Shiva statue and, for those with an extra day, Jog Falls.

overview.text:
Udupi, Karnataka's 'Temple City', grew around the 13th-century Sri Krishna Matha and the eight Ashta Mathas of Madhvacharya. It gave the world sattvic Udupi cuisine and its crisp dosas, and it is the heartland of Yakshagana theatre and the winter Kambala buffalo races.

On the coast are Malpe Beach, the ferry to St Mary's Island's basalt columns, and Kaup's old lighthouse.

how_to_reach.text: Mangaluru airport is about 60 km away. Udupi station, about 3 km from the temple, has trains to Bengaluru, Mumbai and Mangaluru.

best_time.text: October to March, with October–February the peak season.

itineraries.title: Bengaluru in 2 days: gardens, food and Nandi Hills
itineraries.summary: A breakfast trail, Lalbagh and Cubbon Park on day one; sunrise at Nandi Hills and Bangalore Palace on day two.
itineraries.seoDescription: Two days in Bengaluru: Brahmins' Coffee Bar and Vidyarthi Bhavan, Lalbagh's Glass House, Cubbon Park, VV Puram, sunrise at Nandi Hills and Bangalore Palace.

plan.overview: Bengaluru is best enjoyed slowly — eat early, walk the gardens, and get out of town once for sunrise.
plan.transport: Metro and autos in town; a cab for Nandi Hills.
plan.season: Nandi Hills is best September to February.

days.title: Day 1: Breakfast trail and gardens
days.summary:
Morning: idli-vade at Brahmins' Coffee Bar, then masale dose at Vidyarthi Bhavan.

Afternoon: Lalbagh and its Glass House, then Cubbon Park.

Evening: street food at VV Puram.

days.title: Day 2: Nandi Hills sunrise and the palace
days.summary: Leave before dawn for sunrise at Nandi Hills (opens 6 am). Back in town, tour Bangalore Palace (10 am–5:30 pm).
days.travel: Bengaluru to Nandi Hills about 60 km by road.

budget.assumptions: VacayOut lists only fees it could check with an official source; hotels, transport and meals are not estimated. Check current prices before you book.

booking.detail: Check it isn't closed for an event before you go.

alternatives: Add Mysuru as a two-day side trip.
Swap Nandi Hills for ISKCON on Hare Krishna Hill.
tips: Carry a light layer for Nandi Hills at dawn.

itineraries.title: Mysuru in 2 days: palace, Chamundi Hills and Srirangapatna
itineraries.summary: The palace, art gallery and market on day one (ideally a Sunday for the lights); Chamundi Hills and Srirangapatna on day two.
itineraries.seoDescription: Two days in Mysuru: Mysuru Palace and its illumination, Jaganmohan Palace, Devaraja Market, Chamundi Hills and Tipu Sultan's Srirangapatna.

plan.overview: Plan day one for a Sunday or holiday so you can see the palace lit up in the evening.
plan.transport: Autos in town; a cab for Chamundi Hills and Srirangapatna.
plan.season: October for Dasara; November to February for quieter days.

days.title: Day 1: Palace, gallery and market
days.summary:
Morning: Mysuru Palace at opening (10 am).

Afternoon: Jaganmohan Palace's art gallery, then Devaraja Market.

Evening: the palace illumination, 7–8 pm on Sundays and holidays.
days.travel: Bengaluru to Mysuru about 3.5 hours by road.

days.title: Day 2: Chamundi Hills and Srirangapatna
days.summary:
Morning: Chamundi Hills and the Nandi on the steps.

Afternoon: Srirangapatna — the Ranganathaswamy Temple, the fort, the Gumbaz and Daria Daulat Bagh.

budget.assumptions: VacayOut lists only fees it could check with an official source; hotels, transport and meals are not estimated. Check current prices before you book.

tips: Wear slip-on shoes — they come off at the palace.

itineraries.title: Coorg in 3 days: falls, coffee hills and a monastery
itineraries.summary: Madikeri's falls and viewpoints, elephants at Dubare and the Golden Temple, then a trek up Tadiandamol.
itineraries.seoDescription: Three days in Coorg: Abbey Falls, Raja's Seat, Omkareshwara Temple, Dubare Elephant Camp, Namdroling Monastery and the Tadiandamol trek.

plan.overview: Base yourself in Madikeri; day two heads east to Dubare and Bylakuppe, day three into the hills.
plan.transport: A car with driver is easiest; buses link the main towns.

days.title: Day 1: Madikeri
days.summary:
Morning: Abbey Falls (open from 9 am).

Afternoon: the Omkareshwara Temple.

Evening: sunset at Raja's Seat.
days.travel: Bengaluru to Madikeri about 250 km by road.

days.title: Day 2: Dubare and Bylakuppe
days.summary:
Morning: elephants bathing at Dubare.

Afternoon: the Namdroling Monastery at Bylakuppe.

days.title: Day 3: Tadiandamol
days.summary: Trek Tadiandamol from Nalaknad Palace, Kodagu's highest peak at 1,748 m.

budget.assumptions: VacayOut lists only fees it could check with an official source; hotels, transport and meals are not estimated. Check current prices before you book.

booking.detail: Book a coffee-estate homestay for the full Coorg experience.

alternatives: Swap the trek for Iruppu Falls in the south.
tips: Carry rain gear outside the dry season.

itineraries.title: Hampi in 3 days: ruins, temples and coracles
itineraries.summary: The sacred centre and Matanga Hill, then the Vittala Temple and a coracle ride, then the Royal Enclosure.
itineraries.seoDescription: Three days in Hampi: Virupaksha Temple, Hemakuta Hill and Matanga Hill sunset, the Vittala Temple and Stone Chariot, a coracle ride and the Royal Enclosure.

plan.overview: Karnataka Tourism suggests about three days for Hampi — this plan walks the sacred centre, the river and the royal core in turn.
plan.transport: Bicycles, mopeds or autos between sites.

days.title: Day 1: Sacred centre and Matanga Hill
days.summary:
Morning: the Virupaksha Temple.

Afternoon: Hemakuta Hill and the monolithic Ganeshas.

Evening: sunset from Matanga Hill.
days.travel: Overnight bus or train from Bengaluru to Hosapete, then 13 km to Hampi.

days.title: Day 2: Vittala Temple and the river
days.summary:
Morning: the Vittala Temple, Stone Chariot and musical pillars.

Late afternoon: a coracle ride on the Tungabhadra.

days.title: Day 3: Royal Enclosure
days.summary: The Royal Enclosure — Mahanavami Dibba, Stepped Tank, Lotus Mahal and Elephant Stables — early or late for soft light.

budget.assumptions: VacayOut lists only fees it could check with an official source; hotels, transport and meals are not estimated. Check current prices before you book.

booking.detail: Book the overnight train or KSRTC bus to Hosapete early.

alternatives: Continue to Badami, about 140 km away.
tips: Carry water, a hat and sunscreen.
Wear a life jacket on the coracle.

itineraries.title: Badami, Pattadakal and Aihole in 2 days
itineraries.summary: Badami's caves, fort and lake on day one; the Chalukya temples of Pattadakal and Aihole on day two.
itineraries.seoDescription: Two days on the Chalukya trail: Badami's cave temples, fort and Agastya Lake, then Pattadakal's UNESCO temples and Aihole's Durga Temple.

plan.overview: One day for Badami town, one for the surrounding circuit — Karnataka Tourism's own suggestion.
plan.transport: Walk in Badami; a car or bus to Pattadakal and Aihole.

days.title: Day 1: Badami
days.summary:
Morning: the four cave temples (open 6 am).

Midday: climb to Badami Fort.

Evening: Agastya Lake and the Bhutanatha temples.
days.travel: Hubballi airport is about 105 km away; overnight buses run from Bengaluru.

days.title: Day 2: Pattadakal and Aihole
days.summary:
Morning: Pattadakal's temple group, 22 km away.

Afternoon: Aihole and its Durga Temple.

budget.assumptions: VacayOut lists only fees it could check with an official source; hotels, transport and meals are not estimated. Check current prices before you book.

booking.detail: Hire a car for day two to fit both sites in comfortably.

alternatives: Combine with Hampi for a north Karnataka heritage trip.
tips: Start at dawn — it gets very hot by noon.
Wear sturdy shoes for the fort climb.

itineraries.title: Gokarna in 3 days: temple, beaches and day trips

itineraries.seoDescription: Three days in Gokarna: Mahabaleshwar Temple, Kudle and Om beaches, the trek to Paradise Beach, Mirjan Fort and Murudeshwar.

plan.overview: Temple first, beaches second, day trip third — a classic Gokarna pattern.
plan.transport: Walk and boats between beaches; a taxi for day trips.

days.title: Day 1: Temple and town
days.summary: Early darshan at the Mahabaleshwar Temple (from 6 am), then Kudle Beach; sunset on Main Beach.
days.travel: Overnight bus from Bengaluru, or train to Gokarna Road, Ankola or Kumta.

days.title: Day 2: Beach trek
days.summary: Om Beach in the morning, then trek over the headlands to Half Moon and Paradise; return by boat.

days.title: Day 3: Mirjan Fort and Murudeshwar
days.summary: Mirjan Fort in the morning, then Murudeshwar's Shiva statue and gopura.

budget.assumptions: VacayOut lists only fees it could check with an official source; hotels, transport and meals are not estimated. Check current prices before you book.

booking.detail: October to March books out fast — reserve ahead.

alternatives: Swap day three for the Yana rocks.
Add a Netrani dive from Murudeshwar (October to May).
tips: Don't swim at Main Beach — strong currents.

itineraries.title: Karnataka heritage trail in 8 days: Bengaluru to Badami
itineraries.summary: Bengaluru's gardens, Mysuru's palace and Srirangapatna, three days in Hampi, and the Chalukya caves and temples around Badami.
itineraries.seoDescription: Eight days across Karnataka: Bengaluru, Mysuru Palace and Srirangapatna, Hampi's Vijayanagara ruins, and Badami, Pattadakal and Aihole.

plan.overview: From the capital south to Mysuru, then north by overnight train or bus to Hampi and on to the Chalukya heartland.
plan.transport: Trains, overnight buses and cabs; a car with driver from Hampi to Badami.
plan.season: October to February suits the whole route.

days.title: Day 1: Bengaluru
days.summary: Breakfast trail, Lalbagh and Cubbon Park.

days.title: Day 2: Mysuru Palace
days.summary: Drive to Mysuru; the palace in the afternoon and, on a Sunday, the lights at 7 pm.
days.travel: Bengaluru to Mysuru about 3.5 hours by road.

days.title: Day 3: Chamundi Hills and Srirangapatna
days.summary: Chamundi Hills early, Srirangapatna in the afternoon; overnight train or bus north.

days.title: Day 4: Hampi's sacred centre
days.summary: The Virupaksha Temple, Hemakuta Hill and sunset on Matanga Hill.

days.title: Day 5: Vittala Temple and the river
days.summary: The Stone Chariot and musical pillars, then a coracle ride.

days.title: Day 6: Royal Enclosure, then Badami
days.summary: The Royal Enclosure in the morning; drive to Badami (about 140 km) in the afternoon.
days.travel: Hampi to Badami about 140 km by road.

days.title: Day 7: Badami
days.summary: The cave temples at dawn, the fort, and Agastya Lake at sunset.

days.title: Day 8: Pattadakal and Aihole
days.summary: Pattadakal in the morning, Aihole in the afternoon, then on to Hubballi.

tips: Start sightseeing early to beat the heat in the north.

guides.title: Best time to visit Karnataka
guides.summary: When to go to Hampi, Badami, Mysuru, Coorg and the coast — and the festivals worth planning around.
guides.seoTitle: Best Time to Visit Karnataka: Season Guide
guides.seoDescription: When to visit Karnataka: October–February for Hampi, Badami, Coorg and the coast, October for Mysuru Dasara, and the monsoon for Jog Falls.

body.intro: For most of Karnataka, the cool, dry months from October to February are the sweet spot.

sections.heading: Heritage sites
sections.text: Hampi is best from October to February; Badami too, at 18–28°C, while March to May often tops 40°C.

sections.heading: Mysuru
sections.text: October brings Dasara — the most rewarding month despite the crowds. November to February is quieter and pleasant.

sections.heading: Hills and coast
sections.text: Coorg is cool and clear from October to February. Gokarna's season is October to March, when the sea is calm; Udupi's peak is October–February.

sections.heading: Monsoon
sections.text: The monsoon closes Gokarna's beaches for swimming, but Jog Falls is at its thundering best during and just after the rains.

guides.seoDescription: Plan Hampi: the Vittala Temple's Stone Chariot, Virupaksha Temple, the Royal Enclosure, Matanga Hill, coracle rides, getting there and when to go.

body.intro: Hampi rewards slow exploring. Here is how to see the best of it in about three days.

sections.heading: Why Hampi
sections.text: The Vijayanagara capital, founded in 1336, was among the largest and richest cities in the world. Its more than 1,600 surviving monuments have been a UNESCO site since 1986.

items.title: Vittala Temple
items.body: The Stone Chariot (on the ₹50 note) and 56 musical pillars.

items.title: Virupaksha Temple
items.body: A living temple with a 50 m gopuram.

items.title: Royal Enclosure
items.body: Mahanavami Dibba, the Stepped Tank, Lotus Mahal and Elephant Stables.

items.title: Matanga Hill
items.body: The best sunset in central Hampi.

sections.heading: On the river
sections.text: Round bamboo coracles leave from ghats near the Virupaksha and Kodandarama temples; life jackets are mandatory.

sections.heading: Planning
sections.text: Hosapete Junction is about 13 km away. Come from October to February and allow about three days.

guides.title: Mysuru Dasara guide: the palace lights and the Jamboo Savari
guides.summary: What happens at Mysuru Dasara, its history, and how to plan a visit.
guides.seoTitle: Mysuru Dasara Guide: Jamboo Savari & Palace Lights
guides.seoDescription: Plan Mysuru Dasara: the 10-day Nada Habba, the illuminated palace, the Jamboo Savari with the 750 kg golden howdah, and its history.

body.intro: Dasara is Mysuru at its most magnificent — and its busiest.

sections.heading: The festival
sections.text: Mysuru Dasara, Karnataka's state festival, lasts 10 days. In 2026 it ran from 11 to 21 October.

sections.heading: Jamboo Savari
sections.text: On Vijayadashami, a procession leaves the palace courtyard; an elephant carries the goddess Chamundeshwari in the 750 kg golden howdah.

sections.heading: The palace lights
sections.text: During Dasara the palace's roughly 97,000 bulbs burn for two hours every night.

sections.heading: History
sections.text: Vijayanagara rulers began the festival in the 14th century; Raja Wadiyar I revived it in 1610 at Srirangapatna.

guides.summary: Gokarna's five beaches, the trek that links them, safety tips and when to go.

guides.seoDescription: Gokarna's beaches: Main, Kudle, Om, Half Moon and Paradise, the 2–4 hour beach trek, swimming safety and the October–March season.

body.intro: Gokarna's coast is a string of coves joined by a cliff path.

items.title: Main Beach
items.body: By the temple; for sunsets, not swimming — strong currents.

items.title: Kudle
items.body: The largest, 10 minutes' walk from town.

items.title: Om
items.body: Shaped like 'Om'; water sports and dolphin trips.

items.title: Paradise
items.body: The most remote; on foot or by boat from Om.

sections.heading: The trek
sections.text: Kudle to Om, Half Moon and Paradise takes 2–4 hours over rocky headlands. Wear sturdy shoes and carry water.

sections.heading: When to go
sections.text: October to March, when the sea is calm. In the monsoon the beaches close for swimming.

body.intro: Coorg is about slowing down among coffee estates and misty hills.

sections.heading: The region
sections.text: Kodagu, the 'Scotland of India', is home to the Kodava community, which gave India Field Marshal Cariappa and General Thimayya.
